item.title: Leitrim open Lidl league with victory
item.description: The 2026 Lidl National Football League got under way on Sunday with four games in Division 4 of the competition. Six players found the net as Leitrim, one of the promotion favourites, ousted neighbours Longford by 6-17 to 2-10 at Glennon Brothers Pearse Park. Leitrim, with goals from Vivienne Egan, Leah Fox and Kate Gormley, led 3-5 to 1-6 at the interval. item.title: St Brigid’s beaten at the death in All-Ireland thriller
item.description: A spirited Brigid’s display which seen Ruaidhri Fallon score a goal and six points wasn’t enough in a dramatic final. A last ditch Mikey Geaney point clinched the Andy Merrigan Cup for the Kerry Champions. Dingle started the stronger racing into a four point lead with points from Tom O’Sullivan and Niall Geaney either side of a Billy O’Connor two pointer. item.title: Carrick cinema to reopen soon under new chain
item.description: Carrick-on-Shannon cinema is to reopen under a new chain that has cinemas in Donegal. The Carrick facility has been closed for the past couple of weeks after it was sold. Construction work is now under way. Advertisement Eclipse Cinemas, which has outlets in Bundoran and Lifford, says it will reopen soon. item.title: Mullooly has 'serious concerns' for Mercosur deal after new Trump tariffs
item.description: A local MEP says he’s less confident the Mercosur deal will be rejected after Donald Trump’s actions over the weekend. The US president warned levies will be placed on goods from countries who want to block his takeover of Greenland – until he secures a deal to buy the arctic island from Denmark. He says he'll impose 10-per cent tariffs on products imported from the UK and seven other European countries from February the 1st. item.title: Roscommon paired with Slovenia for Ireland's EU presidency
item.description: A local councillor has welcomed Roscommon's pairing with Slovenia during Ireland's EU presidency. Minister for Foreign Affairs Helen McEntee announced the details, which aim to engage communities across the country on Ireland's European relationships. In each county in the state, the ambassadors will participate in a range of public events to strengthen their ties with European countries. item.title: Minister Peter Burke meets tourism leaders to discuss 2026 priorities
item.description: Tourism Minister and Longford-Westmeath TD, Peter Burke, is meeting with 600 tourism industry leaders from around the country to highlight priorities for the year ahead. It kickstarts a new marketing strategy by Tourism Ireland which plans to grow the overseas visitor spend for the island of Ireland to €10 billion euro annually by 2031.
